title: Drugs & Medicines
whatItIs: Illegal drugs and some medicines can make you unsafe to drive. Driving while impaired by either is against the law.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive under the influence of drugs or medicine.
You MUST NOT drive with certain drugs in your blood above set limits, even if you feel fine.

keyFacts: Even over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Read the label to see if they may affect it.
Check with your doctor or pharmacist, and don't drive if you're advised you may be impaired.
Drug-driving penalties include at least a 1-year ban, an unlimited fine and a criminal record.

items.title: Illegal drugs
items.text: Never drive after taking them. Their effects are unpredictable.

items.title: Medicines
items.text: Ask your doctor or pharmacist. Don't drive if you're told you may be impaired.

items.title: Not sure?
items.text: Ask your doctor or pharmacist before you drive.

items.title: Roadside tests
items.text: The police can test you for drugs at the roadside.

b.label: Medicines
points: Can be fine to drive on
Only if they don't impair you

onTheTest.question: Your doctor has prescribed a new medicine. What should you do before you drive?
options: Check if it is safe to drive while taking it
onTheTest.why: Some medicines affect your driving. Read the label, check with your doctor or pharmacist, and don't drive if you're advised you may be impaired.

traps: Legal medicines can still make your driving illegal if they impair you.
Over-the-counter medicines count too: if they make you unfit to drive, it's illegal.
Feeling fine doesn't mean you are under the drug-driving limit.
